records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.min(1)`, so a caller invoking the endpoint directly (bypassing the web dialog's own client-side guard) with `guests: []` is accepted by validation and only fails downstream with the misleading BAD_REQUEST message "emails_must_be_unique_valid", which describes a different condition (duplicate/invalid emails) than "no guests supplied"
records.rationale: Verified from the diff: addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.min(1)`, and the handler in addGuests.handler.ts throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })` when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, which is exactly the path an empty array takes. So a direct API caller with `guests: []` gets a misleading message. This is a real, specific gap (missing schema-level constraint plus a confusing error message), but it does not cause incorrect behavior or data issues — validation eventually rejects the input — so it's a substantive
